On vote 328 I wonder if I could ask the minister what is now the present position of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police building at Port Saunders, Newfoundland?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: We shall look that up and get the answer.

While the minister is getting the answer to that question I should like to ask questions about one or two other places. Can the minister give me any information about the proposed Royal Canadian Mounted Police building for Corner Brook, Newfoundland? This item was announced last fall and later withdrawn. I was hoping at that time that the minister would carry on with the construction of this proposed building at Corner Brook and regard the building as a winter works project at a time when unemployment is rather high in that city.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext:
Our difficulty is that we build for the R.C.M.P. when we are asked to do so, and if the Minister of Justice were here I could give the hon. member an answer. I would be happy to obtain that information and pass it on to the hon. member, but it really does not form part of the estimates.
Supply-Public Works

I recognize the correctness of what the minister says, but I ask this question on the basis of the fact that the minister announced last fall that this building would be built and it was he who later announced that the program was cancelled for the time being. It is in the light of that statement that I ask him my question now.
Is it agreeable that this item should stand for the time being?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: I am sorry, but even if I had the answer for the hon. member, the expenditure would still not form part of these estimates. I will undertake to get the information from the Minister of Justice and I will give it to the hon. member tomorrow. Would that be satisfactory?
That would be satisfactory.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Item agreed to.
331. New Brunswick, $765,000.

Early this afternoon I asked the minister to give us some information in connection with the public building under construction at the present time in Camp-bellton, New Brunswick. What I want to know is on what date was construction started; what progress has been made to date; has there been any delays during the construction, and what were the reasons for such delays? Were any additional costs involved besides the contract which was awarded for the building? I have further questions to ask in connection with this particular item. I think the minister should be in a position to give me this information because it comes under his department, and in item 331 there is an amount of $100,000 to complete the building which I have mentioned.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext:
I am sorry about the delay. The date of the award of the contract is September 11, 1958; the amount of the contract was $307,000, and it was awarded to Kenney Construction Company Limited. The work on the Campbellton, New Brunswick, public building is now about 86 per cent completed; it will be completed, we hope, in 1960. No extras have been asked for by the Kenney Construction Company in regard to the contract which they signed. However, the department has made some changes in the public building as the result of subsequent representations as to the plans of the building. As a result, the department has agreed to pay for these extras, shall we say, by a supplementary contract for $16,172.30. There have been no extras on the contract awarded to the original contractor, the Kenney Construction Company, for the original work to be done.

Supply-Public Works

I want to follow up my questions about this particular building because on January 20 of this year I placed the following questions on the order paper:
Were tenders called for the construction of the federal building at Campbellton, New Brunswick?
The reply was:
Yes, on August 18, 1958.
My second question was:
If so: (a) what was the amount of the lowest tender?
The reply was $307,000. My next question was:
(b) To whom was the contract awarded, and at what amount?
The reply was:
Kenney Construction Company Limited, Yarmouth, Nova Scotia, at $307,000.
My next question was:
Has work been started and at what date?
The answer was:
Yes, on October 1, 1958.
This is just an ordinary building to cost $300,000, which has been under construction for almost two years and it is not yet completed. I was not satisfied with the reply which I received from the minister to my questions and I came back again on February 2 and asked the following questions:
Is the Department of Public Works spending any amount of money on the federal public building at Campbellton, New Brunswick, in addition to the amount awarded to the contractor as per his original contract?
The answer was "yes". My second question was:
If so, what is the additional amount (a) spent to date; (b) estimated to be spent before the building is completed?
The answer was, $411.80. Today the minister advises the house that the department has agreed to pay an additional amount of $16,172 for changes in planning. The answer to the second part of my question was:
No additional expenditure anticipated.
These answers were given on February 2, a year and a half after the work had been started on that particular building. My third question was:
Have there been any delays in the construction since October 1, 1958?
The reply was "yes". My fourth question was:
What were the reasons of such delays? Have such delays occasioned additional cost and to what amount?
The reply to the first part was:
Defective concrete and damages resulting from freezing action during the placing of the concrete.

The reply to the second part was "no". It is a well known fact, that for reasons known to the minister and to the department the work on the public building in Campbellton was delayed considerably. After the building had been framed, after the steel structure was put up, after parts of the walls had been erected, after part of the plumbing had been installed, it was noticed that the building was sinking. The building had been erected over and above a frog pond and it was sinking four or five inches.

speakerposition: Minister of National Health and Welfare
speechtext: Almost like the printing bureau.

The minister knows something about it; that is why I want to bring it to the attention of the committee. This has taken place under the minister's administration. The work was stopped. Part of the plumbing that had been installed was dismantled; cement pilings were put under the building at a cost which I have good reason to believe was well over $16,000, referred to by the minister. This committee has a right to know the facts about this building. I want the minister to advise the committee whether it is true that it was found that this building which was being built over what is known in Campbellton as a frog pond was built without proper soundings having been taken and that the additional cost may reach the figure of $50,000, or even more. I do not know, but I want to find out from the minister what is the total expenditure? The changes which have been made for the additional amount of $16,000, according to the minister, were changes in planning. There is quite a difference between additional costs for planning and additional costs because the proper borings had not been done by the department to satisfy itself that the foundation was being placed on solid ground; that water was not running under the building and that the building was not sinking after it had been partly constructed.
We have a right to know the details about this building; we have a right to know why on February 2, after all this work or 90 per cent of the extra work had been done, I was told in the house that no additional expenditure was anticipated for that building. I have further questions but I want a reply to the questions I have asked so far before I proceeed further.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext:
I think I have given the answer. As a matter of fact, I did not tell my hon. friend this, for whom the public building is being erected in Gloucester and it is not necessary for him to be so vehement,

vindictive and arbitrary. After all, the government of Canada is constructing a building for his constituents.
It is not in his constituency.
On a point of order, it is not in my riding.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: Is it not in your riding?
No, it is in Restigouche county.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: Then that is the explanation for the arrogance the hon. member has shown. In any event, just control yourself or I will answer in kind.
Oh, oh.

Is this a threat from the
minister?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: My friend, the whip across the way, is shaking his finger at me. We have an agreement-no threats. The bad foundation about which the hon. member for Gloucester is complaining was paid for in full by the contractor. I think it cost him $60,000 extra. He had to pay that himself and this amount of $16,172.30 is what we decided should be added afterwards.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, the hon. member for Gloucester has asked the minister if he can explain what on the face of it seems like gross inefficiency in the construction of a public building and in asking that question he is accused of being arrogant.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: I never heard the Leader of the Opposition talk like that and I am sure the hon. member for Golucester has not followed the example of the Leader of the Opposition.
Mr. Chairman, I think the Minister of Public Works should be the last member in the house to use the word "arrogant" in view of his past record in the house. I asked straightforward questions.

speakerposition: Minister of National Health and Welfare
speechtext:
And you got the
answers.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: Just take it easy.

I want straightforward answers to my questions. I would say that the answers I have received from the minister contradict the information I received in answer to questions I placed on the order paper on January 20 and again on February 2 of this year. Is the government trying to hide the facts? I am concerned about the taxpayers' money just as much as is the minister. I knew that additional money was being spent and I wanted to find out who was
Supply-Pub lie Works paying the cost and what amount was involved. The minister now says that the contractor has been called upon to pay $60,000 extra with regard to work which had not been properly planned by the department. I think it is not right to ask any contractor to assume such an additional charge. The minister should at least explain to the house why on February 2, 1960 he informed the house that no additional expenditures were anticipated outside of an amount of $411.80 which he stated was being paid to the contractor for additional work.

The minister has not answered the hon. member's question. On the 2nd of February the minister told the house in answer to a question that some $411 was being spent on the project. He has told us tonight that an additional $16,172 is being spent. There is a considerable difference between $411 and $16,172. I want to be very careful to explain this as the minister explained it. The minister said, I think, that the department had decided on changing the plans and that this was in effect a second contract. I think the committee should be told at what date they decided to change the plans, what was the reason for doing so and when the tender was called for this additional work and, if not, how they arrived at this figure and whether on February 2 when the hon. member was told that no additional expense was anticipated they had no inkling whatever of this extra $16,172.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: My friend is quite right. I think the question is properly asked and it is a very simple one. The original return was made in February, was it not?
February 2.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: At that time no other change was anticipated by the government but in June a decision was made which went to treasury board and on June 29 permission was obtained for a series of changes to be made. I might say that this was done by the government of its own volition and not at the request of the contractor. It does not form any part of the original contract.

Again I want to follow up a question I asked on February 2. At that time I asked whether there had been any delays in the construction since October 1, 1958. That was a straightforward question. The reply I received was, yes. I also asked what were the reasons for such delays and the answer I received was there was defective concrete and damages resulting from freezing action during the placing of the concrete.
The minister has just admitted that the contractor had to do $60,000 worth of additional work and I have every reason to believe

Supply-Public Works that on February 2 that extra work had been completed by the contractor, and that that was the reason for the delay. The minister cannot tell me, having regard to the fact that this is a $300,000 building which was started almost two years ago and is only 86 per cent complete, that there has not been unreasonable delay. Why did they try to hide information with respect to the straightforward questions which I placed on the order paper?
I should like to ask the minister another question. He said that the contractor had been involved in an additional expenditure of $60,000. Is there any correspondence with the department from the contractor claiming part or all of this amount?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: The contractor certainly asked us to pay. In fact, he insisted that we should pay. He was in the office from time to time and I believe there is some correspondence on the subject. However, we insisted that the fault was his and that he should pay and so he paid the $60,000 himself, which was all included in the original contract price I gave the hon. member at the beginning.

speakerposition: Minister of National Health and Welfare
speechtext: There were no extras like under the previous government.

The Minister of National
Health and Welfare has anticipated a question of mine that the minister did not answer. Why were these changes in the plans made? I presume there was some purpose in spending the extra $16,000. Could the minister say what the purpose was and why it was not anticipated when the original tenders were called?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext:
Keeping in mind that the
$60,000 was paid by the construction company and not by us, we ordered the extras because of a decision we made that there should be differences in partitions as well as differences in the basement and these amounted to $16,172.30.

Can the minister say what was the purpose of these differences in partitions and differences in the basement and why they were not foreseen under the general principles he has laid down that such things should always be foreseen by the department before the original tender is called? Who was responsible for the lack of foresight?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: My friend is getting back to the $60,000-
I am talking about the $16,000.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: The Liberal administration would have paid the $60,000; we did not.

That is another of the minister's typical answers.
[Mr. Robichaud.l

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext: That is a typical answer.
It has nothing to do with the question.
A complete answer.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext: That is why we are still on the minister's estimates.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: The answer in regard to the other matter is this: There should be no criticism by my hon. friend if the government decided later on to make some substantial change which is merited and which is going to improve the building. There could be no fault to find because it has not cost anything extra. The extra work is being done by providing the partitions and the building is being improved. It is not costing the taxpayers any more.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: But they are getting in return an improved building for $16,000 extra. Does my hon. friend from Bonavista-Twillingate not understand that?
No, I do not and I should like it explained.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: Of course, none are so blind as those who will not see.

I must say that when I build something, and I have had some recent experience in building, and then I decide to make a change in my building which is going to cost, if my arithmetic is correct, over 5 per cent of the total cost, I think twice about whether those improvements are worth the extra cost. The minister has not said one word to indicate what these improvements were, or why the necessity for them could not have been foreseen originally.

The minister has stated that the department has refused the contractor, Kenney, his claim of $60,000. Has the matter been finally settled or is there still an opening for Kenney to claim a certain amount from the department?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: That is a fair question. So far as we are concerned, it is like the payment of the sum which the Liberals would have us pay Mr. Cormier, that $55,000. We are not going to pay it and I as Minister of Public Works invite him to sue us for it. I also invite Kenney to sue us. The matter has been finally settled, so far as we are concerned, and we are not going to pay.
Will the minister say whether or not the departmental engineers made borings on this site to satisfy themselves this was a good site before the property was bought and the building started?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext:
I have no idea. In reply to the hon. member for Levis who asked for the total staff of the district architect and the office of the property building management, may I say that in 1959-60 there were 727; 1960-61, 734, an increase of seven. The supervisors in 1959-60 number 14 and in
1960-61, 14. The foremen in 1959-60 numbered 19, and in 1960-61, 18.
Did I hear correctly when the minister said there were 774 employees?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: No, in 1959-60, 727 employees in the district architects office in Montreal.
And that includes everyone in that office?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: It also includes the property and building management. The district architects staff cannot be distinguished. Would the hon. member like me to find out how many are allocated to the district architects?
Yes.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
speechtext: The hon. member asked for the answer which I am now giving. If he wants me to segregate that, I will have that information for him tomorrow morning.
Thank you.

QUETICO PARK, ONT.  IMPORT OF U.S. OUTFITTERS EQUIPMENT
speechtext:
1.	Has the government received protests from any person, persons, or associations regarding the import of United States outfitters equipment to the Quetico park area?
2.	If so, from whom, to what effect?
3.	What action was taken as a result of such protests?
Answer by: Hon. Leon Balcer (Acting Secretary of State):
1.	Yes.
2.	Protests were received from William Benidickson, M.P., on behalf of Thunder Bay district tourist operators association; Fort William and Port Arthur, Ontario; John Richardson, Saganaga Lake, Ontario; northern Ontario tourist outfitters association; Roger Thew, Kawene, Ontario; and from F. A. Mac-Dougall, deputy minister of lands and forests, province of Ontario, on behalf of the northern Ontario tourist outfitters association.
3.	The advice given in reply to these protests was that non-residents of Canada are entitled under the regulations made pursuant to the Customs Act to import temporarily boats, canoes, sporting and camping equipment for health or pleasure purposes, whether such articles are their personal property or are on hire from commercial outfitters. It was pointed out that this privilege is not available to residents of Canada.
